chapter: Trombone technique, plunger mute and the California years
title: A famous trombonist in Hawaii and Sandy Williams's badly fitted teeth
summary: He praises an unnamed famous trombonist living in Hawaii, and says Sandy Williams stopped playing over an improper fit, urging musicians to find a dentist who understands them.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Trombone, too. Don't forget that. There's a very famous one. I won't name the name, because he probably don't want nobody to know that he... But he brags to me about it. But maybe he don't want anybody to know. So there you go. He ain't got a child in the yard up there, but he still... [LAUGHS] You know what I mean? He still makes the scene, man! And beautiful. Sounds as good as he did, if not better.
Do you think maybe off the record we could say who he was?
Oh, you would know who he was. He lives in Hawaii. Should I say any more?
Oh yeah, he's...
Beautiful!
Out in Colorado he sounded very good.

Sure. Plays just as good, if not better. I dig him. I think he's beautiful. And there's a guy named Sandy Williams. Poor Sandy. He's scared to blow because he's scared of his teeth. But he got an improper fit. See, you must have a proper fit made. You've got to make your
* e.g., Trummy Young
Dickenson - 77

mouth look as it when you had teeth, you know, and have the guy to fix those teeth so that your nose is the same distance from your chin as it was at first. You know? But they give them these little-bitty mice teeth, little-bitty teeth, and make your mouth too short, and then you can't... You can't work that that way. You ain't got enough chops for the big mouthpiece. So if you could get a dentist that's interested... You've got to get a dentist interested in your particular mouth.
A dentist who realizes that you're a musician.
That that's your livelihood. You know?
Yeah, Sandy was a hell of a trombone player, too.

Sure, he was. And he still could be. He just put his horn down because he got scared he couldn't play. So if you don't play... How are you going to play if you don't play? You know...[LAUGHS] All you've got to do is get the right fit teeth. Don't let 'em just slam anything to you. Say, "No, this ain't right, man. Fix them. Make those teeth a little bigger. And make my mouth and nose so that I won't look all scrunched up in the mouth," you know. You know what I mean?
Mmm-hmm.
I mean, give me some sturdy teeth, because you've got to have them sturdy. Do you know what I mean?
Dickenson - 78
It can be done. It's been done, and it is done.
Well, they do those things better now than they used to.
Sure, they do. And there should be no problem any more.
